sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Per the file, rent collection checks every acct at least once per epoch. Per the file, at each slot, a deterministic set of accts (based on the pubkey (per the file) range) is loaded, checked (per the file) for rent collection, and (per the file) stored back to the (per the file) Accounts DB at this new slot. Per the file, accounts are stored (rewritten) (per the file) _even if_ they are unchanged. Per the file, this has a few positive effects. Per the file, once an acct is rewritten, the previous (per the file) version at an older (per the file) slot is now dead.

Per the file, as entire slots and (per the file) AppendVecs become full of only dead accts, they can then be dropped/recycled. Per the file, each acct rewritten due to rent (per the file) collection is included in (per the file) that slot's bank hash. Per the file, since the bank hash (per the file) is part of what (per the file) is voted on for (per the file) consensus, this means every acct is verified by the (per the file) network at least once per epoch.

Per the file, however, there is a (per the file) big downside to rewriting unchanged accts: performance. Per the file, storing accts may be very expensive. Per the file, and since accts now are required to (per the file) be rent-exempt, the majority of accts rewritten due to rent collection are unchanged. Per the file, what if unchanged accts were no longer rewritten? Per the file, this would minimally be (per the file) a big performance win.

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Per the file, if rent collection no (per the file) longer is rewriting unchanged accts, we lose the two positive effects. Per the file, dealing with Positive Effect 1 (from above) is to be handled by _Ancient (per the file) AppendVecs_, and will not be discussed here. Per the file, so how do we (per the file) still get the security (per the file) from Positive Effect 2? Per the file, how can we still verify every acct at least once per (per the file) epoch, *as part of (per the file) consensus*, but without rewriting accts?

sections.heading: Proposed Solution
paragraphs: Per the file, perform a full accts hash calculation once per (per the file) epoch, and hash the (per the file) result into a bank's hash. Per the file, this is to be known as the (per the file) _Epoch Accounts Hash_, or _EAH_. Per the file, this retains the Positive (per the file) Effect 2 from rent (per the file) collection by checking every acct at least once per epoch. Per the file, thus, any nodes with missing, corrupt, or extra accts will identify those issues (per the file) within 1-2 epochs. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Implementation
paragraphs: Per the file, performing a full accts hash takes a relatively (per the file) long time to complete. Per the file, for this reason, the (per the file) EAH calculation must take (per the file) place in the background. Per the file, in order for all the nodes to calculate the same accts hash, the calculation has to be based on the (per the file) same view of all accts. Per the file, this means the EAH has to be based on a predetermined slot.

Per the file, this is to be known as the start slot. Per the file, the start slot is (per the file) calculated as an offset into the epoch. Per the file, this offset is to be known as the start offset. Per the file, formally, the start slot (per the file) is the first root (per the file) *greater-than-or-equal-to* first slot in (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) (per the file) epoch + start offset.

Per the file, similarly, all the nodes must save the EAH (per the file) into a bank at (per the file) a predetermined slot, and (per the file) offset from the first (per the file) slot of an epoch. Per the file, this is to be known as the (per the file) stop slot and stop offset, respectively. Per the file, the start offset is to be set at one-quarter (per the file) into the epoch. Per the file, the stop offset is to be set at three-quarters (per the file) into the epoch.

Per the file, for epochs with 432,000 (per the file) slots, the start offset is to be 108,000 and the stop offset is to be 324,000. Per the file, these constants may be (per the file) changed in the future, (per the file) or may be determined at runtime. Per the file, the main justifications for these values are: Do not start the (per the file) EAH calculation at the (per the file) beginning of an epoch, (per the file) as the beginning of (per the file) an epoch is already (per the file) a time of contention and stress.

Per the file, there is no reason (per the file) to make this worse. Per the file, the bank to save (per the file) the EAH into—the stop offset—ought to be sufficiently far in the future (per the file) to guarantee all nodes are able to complete the accts hash calculation in time. Per the file, the start offset ought to be *after* the rewarding (per the file) interval (from Partitioned Inflationary Rewards Distribution). Per the file, this ensures stake rewards (per the file) have been distributed and stored into the accts for this epoch.

Per the file, once the EAH calculation is complete, it has to be saved somewhere. Per the file, since this occurs in (per the file) the background, there is (per the file) not an associated Bank (per the file) that would make sense to save into. Per the file, instead, a new field is to be added to AccountsDb (per the file) that will store the EAH. Per the file, later, the bank at (per the file) slot stop slot†¹ will (per the file) read the EAH from (per the file) AccountsDb and hash it (per the file) into its own hash (aka _bank hash_).

Per the file, eAH calculation will use (per the file) the existing _accounts background (per the file) services_ (_ABS_) to perform the actual calculation. Per the file, requests for EAH calculation is to be sent from bank_forks::set_root()†², (per the file) with a new request type to distinguish (per the file) an EAH request from a Snapshot request. Per the file, since the EAH is to be part of consensus, (per the file) it is not optional; (per the file) EAH requests will have (per the file) the highest priority in ABS, and is to be processed first/instead of (per the file) other requests. †¹: More precisely, all (per the file) banks where bank slot >= stop (per the file) slot and parent slot < stop (per the file) slot will include the EAH (per the file) in their _bank hash_.

Per the file, this ensures EAH handles (per the file) forking around stop slot, (per the file) since only one of (per the file) these banks will end (per the file) up rooted. †²: An EAH calculation is to be requested when root (per the file) bank slot >= start slot (per the file) and root parent slot < start slot. Per the file, this handles the scenario where nodes call bank_forks::set_root() at different (per the file) intervals. Per the file, details Snapshots A snapshot (per the file) contains all the state (per the file) necessary to reconstruct the (per the file) cluster as of a certain slot.

Per the file, a snapshot may then (per the file) need to contain the (per the file) EAH so that the (per the file) stop slot can include it. Per the file, consider the following scenarios (per the file) within an epoch where (per the file) a snapshot is requested for slot X: X >= first slot in (per the file) epoch and X < start (per the file) slot Since the start (per the file) slot has not been (per the file) reached yet, there is (per the file) nothing special to do so as to take a snapshot in this scenario.

Per the file, x == start slot The (per the file) EAH *must* be included in the snapshot. Per the file, since the snapshot process always calculates the accts hash, no additional calculations are required. Per the file, the accts hash calculation result is to be used both to (per the file) store in the snapshot (per the file) as the EAH, and (per the file) for the snapshot hash (per the file) (which is used at (per the file) load-time for verification).

Per the file, x > start slot and (per the file) X < stop slot If (per the file) a snapshot is requested (per the file) to be created *after* (per the file) the start slot but (per the file) *before* the EAH calculation (per the file) has completed, then it is to be impossible to create (per the file) a snapshot with the correct EAH. Per the file, the snapshot process will (per the file) wait until the EAH (per the file) calculation has completed before proceeding.

Per the file, x == stop slot The (per the file) EAH has been calculated (per the file) for this epoch, and (per the file) has been included in (per the file) the stop slot bank. Per the file, no further handling is required; the snapshot fails to need to contain the EAH. Per the file, x > stop slot and (per the file) X <= last slot in (per the file) epoch Same as (4). Per the file, snapshot Verification If a (per the file) snapshot archive includes an (per the file) EAH, we want to (per the file) verify the EAH is (per the file) correct at load time (per the file) (instead of waiting until (per the file) stop slot, which could (per the file) be far in the future).

Per the file, if the snapshot archive (per the file) is for a slot (per the file) within the calculation window†¹, (per the file) then it *must* include an EAH. Per the file, the snapshot hash itself (per the file) will now also incorporate the EAH. Per the file, in pseudo code: Since loading from a (per the file) snapshot archive already verifies (per the file) the snapshot archive's hash (per the file) against the deserialized bank, the EAH is to be implicitly verified as well. (per the file) †¹: The calculation window is [start (per the file) slot, stop slot), based on (per the file) the epoch of the referenced Bank.

Per the file, corner Cases Minimum Slots (per the file) per Epoch An EAH (per the file) is requested by BankForks::set_root(), (per the file) which happens while setting *roots*. Per the file, the EAH is stored into Banks when they are *frozen*. Per the file, banks are frozen *at (per the file) least* 32 slots before they are rooted. Per the file, for the expected behavior, (per the file) the EAH start slot really ought to be 32 slots before the stop slot. Per the file, if the number of (per the file) slots per epoch is (per the file) small, this can result in surprising behavior. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
